title: Snipperclips: Cut It Out, Together!
subtitle: Two paper bodies become the tools
summary: Snipperclips: Cut It Out, Together! is SFB Games' cooperative puzzle game, released alongside Switch on 3 March 2017.
body: Snipperclips: Cut It Out, Together! is SFB Games' cooperative puzzle game, released alongside Switch on 3 March 2017. Snip and Clip are paper-like characters whose overlapping bodies can be cut into new shapes. The player uses those changing outlines to solve small physical problems, from fitting a template to carrying an object or popping a balloon. The characters themselves become the equipment, making a puzzle's solution something the players create together rather than an item they simply find in the room.

Rotating and overlapping the two figures determines the shape removed by a snip. A useful hook, cup or sharp point can emerge from the same starting bodies, and the pair must position themselves carefully to produce it. The result also needs to work in motion: a shape that looks promising may handle an object awkwardly once it is carried. The puzzle therefore continues through communication and experimentation, with each attempt showing the players more about the relationship between the outline they made and the task ahead.

The project began as Adam and Tom Vian's Flash prototype Friendshapes before Nintendo helped develop it into a Switch release. The art-supply setting and expressive faces keep failed attempts playful. World mode supports one or two players, while Party and Blitz introduce cooperative and competitive activities for up to four. Calum Bowen composed the music. Sharing the console's controllers suits the idea especially well, placing two people beside one screen where the next cut can be proposed, tested and laughed over immediately. The expanded Snipperclips Plus edition followed on 10 November 2017.
